title: Birthday Problem: Threshold for 99% Match Probability

problemStatement.formal: Find minimal n such that P(n) > 99/100, where P(n) = 1 - 365!/((365^n)*(365-n)!)
problemStatement.plain: Find the minimum number of people needed so that the probability of at least one shared birthday exceeds 99%.
whyMatters: Natural extension of the classic birthday problem
Tests Lean's ability to handle large numeric computations via native_decide

knownResults.goal: Prove the 99% threshold for the birthday problem

currentState.focus: Complete proof verified via Docker build.

knowledge.progressSummary: COMPLETED: Proved birthday problem 99% threshold is n=57 with tight bounds. P(57) > 99/100 and P(56) < 99/100. Docker build verified (22min, native_decide on 146-digit numbers).
insights: native_decide works for 146-digit number comparisons but requires 22min build time
Rational arithmetic with exact fractions avoids floating-point issues

approaches.name: Direct computation via native_decide
approaches.description: Compute exact rational probabilities and verify inequalities via native_decide
